ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: FlowWorks
ModMetaData.author: Mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Dig a channel, let a fluid flow into it: a species- and biome-agnostic engine for canals that carry water, ooze, slime, oil, tar or fuel from a source into the terrain a colonist chooses.
Depth is the primitive. Every excavated cell carries two small integers — D, how far below the surface it was dug (shallow, mid, deep, SUPERDEEP), and F, how much liquid is in it — and everything else is a function of those two on one cell: what it costs to cross, how much it holds, and which liquid surface is drawn. We dig down; we never build up. There is no elevation model, no height advantage, and no fluid simulation: liquid levels itself out on a pulse, by sorting the deepest cells first and letting a full one overflow into whatever has room.
A natural liquid body IS a source — deep terrain that is already full, which is why it spills into a shallower channel dug at its edge. Liquid stays in what has been excavated.
Shipped: the depth/fill grid and its pulse engine (`RM_MapComponent_Excavation`), a dig designator that deepens a cell each time it is used, depth-derived movement cost, a three-tier fill ladder on vanilla's own edge-aware water ramps, and a `FluidDef` describing what a source carries. Water is the one liquid this pass, proving genericity.
A SUPERDEEP excavation is the trapping level and the only one: anything that walks into one falls in and is held there whether the hole is dry or brimming, and gets out only by climbing a ladder somebody built down there. Pull the ladder and they stay. Depth touches shooting in exactly one way, and it is a restriction rather than an advantage — whoever is in a superdeep hole can only trade fire with whoever is standing right at its lip, both directions.
Not yet built, and named so nobody thinks they are missing: sluice gates, burning liquids, and irrigation.
No DLC required. The engine writes the map's temporary terrain layer, which is base-game machinery, and ships its own temporary terrains rather than naming the Odyssey-only ones. Harmony is required, for one patch: the superdeep shooting restriction.
MERGED IN 2026-09-16 (FLOWWORKS_BUILD_PROGRAM_1 Phase 1) — one mod now owns the whole liquid domain, per the owner's ruling that depth is the single primitive underneath all of it:
PITS (was mandrake.rm.pits). The earth that swallows: dig a pit in stages, arm it with a terrain-mimic cover, and enough mass crossing it drops whoever stood there into the hole below. Escape is a struggle clock scored off bodysize, health and manipulation, not a coin flip. The same holder doubles as a gated holding-platform pit cell for prisoners. A pit is not a separate thing from a canal — it is one deep excavation, and a canal is a connected run of shallow ones.
WATER EFFECTS (was mandrake.rm.manywaters). The generic water-effects engine: animated river-steam ambience off a biome's own opt-in extension, RM_DeepSand (impassable, fishable sand built the way vanilla deep water is), and the coloured-water and coloured-slime terrain, fleck and bottle families. Biome-agnostic; the Ash'karr wiring lives in RimUtinni.
LIQUID TYPES (was mandrake.rm.liquidtypes). The liquid registry: per-liquid TerrainDef suites cloned off vanilla water — tar, ooze, propane, acid, brine, coolant, ichor and the rest — plus the RM_LiquidProperties extension the C# reads for what native fields cannot say (pH/corrosion, damage on immersion versus contact).
NOT merged, and staying siblings on the owner's boundary principle — FlowWorks owns what a liquid IS and DOES; a machine that TRANSFORMS one liquid into another is technology: GelatinousSlime (registers rows, keeps its genes), WreckedMachines (distillation and every other conversion), and FloodedCanyon (a flood-driver client).
